description: Joins AI assistant usage (ai_activities) with delivery performance (project_pr_metrics / pull_requests) in single SQL queries, by calendar week and by developer. NOTE: the Project variable filters the DELIVERY side only — ai_activities has no repo or project column, so AI usage is never project-scoped here.

panels.title: Overview — do both sides actually have data?

panels.description: Distinct developers with any AI activity in the time range. COUNT(DISTINCT user_email) is safe across both cursor row grains.

targets.rawSql:
WITH member_emails AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT LOWER(ai.user_email) AS email
  FROM ai_activities ai
  LEFT JOIN accounts acc     ON LOWER(acc.email) = LOWER(ai.user_email)
  LEFT JOIN users u          ON LOWER(u.email)   = LOWER(ai.user_email)
  LEFT JOIN user_accounts ua ON ua.user_id = u.id
  JOIN pull_requests pr
    ON pr.author_id IN (ai.account_id, acc.id, ua.account_id)
  JOIN project_mapping pm
    ON pm.row_id = pr.base_repo_id AND pm.`table` = 'repos'
  WHERE pm.project_name IN ($project)
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_email) AS "AI Active Users"
FROM ai_activities
WHERE $__timeFilter(date)
    AND provider IN ($provider)
  AND user_email <> ''
  AND LOWER(user_email) IN (SELECT email FROM member_emails)

The join — AI usage and delivery on one timeline

panels.description: INNER JOIN of AI usage and PR delivery on calendar week (Monday start). Empty result almost always means the two date ranges do not overlap — widen the time range and set Project to All before suspecting the SQL.

targets.rawSql:
WITH member_emails AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT LOWER(ai.user_email) AS email
  FROM ai_activities ai
  LEFT JOIN accounts acc     ON LOWER(acc.email) = LOWER(ai.user_email)
  LEFT JOIN users u          ON LOWER(u.email)   = LOWER(ai.user_email)
  LEFT JOIN user_accounts ua ON ua.user_id = u.id
  JOIN pull_requests pr
    ON pr.author_id IN (ai.account_id, acc.id, ua.account_id)
  JOIN project_mapping pm
    ON pm.row_id = pr.base_repo_id AND pm.`table` = 'repos'
  WHERE pm.project_name IN ($project)
),
ai AS (
  SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(date) DAY) AS week_start,
         COUNT(DISTINCT user_email) AS ai_users,
         SUM(lines_added)           AS ai_lines,
         SUM(num_sessions)          AS ai_sessions,
         SUM(estimated_cost_usd)    AS ai_cost
  FROM ai_activities
  WHERE $__timeFilter(date)
    AND provider IN ($provider)
    AND user_email <> ''
    AND LOWER(user_email) IN (SELECT email FROM member_emails)
  GROUP BY 1
),
delivery AS (
  SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(pr_merged_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(pr_merged_date) DAY) AS week_start,
         COUNT(*) AS prs_merged,
         AVG(pr_cycle_time) / 60.0 AS avg_cycle_hours
  FROM project_pr_metrics
  WHERE $__timeFilter(pr_merged_date)
    AND project_name IN ($project)
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT ai.week_start                    AS time,
       ai.ai_users                      AS "AI Active Users",
       d.prs_merged                     AS "PRs Merged",
       ROUND(d.avg_cycle_hours, 1)      AS "Avg PR Cycle Time (h)"
FROM ai
INNER JOIN delivery d ON d.week_start = ai.week_start
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Weekly — AI Active Users vs PR Delivery

panels.description: One row per week where BOTH AI usage and merged PRs exist. This is the 'single SQL query across both datasets' deliverable — if this table has rows, the datasets are no longer isolated.

targets.rawSql:
WITH member_emails AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT LOWER(ai.user_email) AS email
  FROM ai_activities ai
  LEFT JOIN accounts acc     ON LOWER(acc.email) = LOWER(ai.user_email)
  LEFT JOIN users u          ON LOWER(u.email)   = LOWER(ai.user_email)
  LEFT JOIN user_accounts ua ON ua.user_id = u.id
  JOIN pull_requests pr
    ON pr.author_id IN (ai.account_id, acc.id, ua.account_id)
  JOIN project_mapping pm
    ON pm.row_id = pr.base_repo_id AND pm.`table` = 'repos'
  WHERE pm.project_name IN ($project)
),
ai AS (
  SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(date) DAY) AS week_start,
         COUNT(DISTINCT user_email) AS ai_users,
         SUM(lines_added)           AS ai_lines,
         SUM(num_sessions)          AS ai_sessions,
         SUM(estimated_cost_usd)    AS ai_cost
  FROM ai_activities
  WHERE $__timeFilter(date)
    AND provider IN ($provider)
    AND user_email <> ''
    AND LOWER(user_email) IN (SELECT email FROM member_emails)
  GROUP BY 1
),
delivery AS (
  SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(pr_merged_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(pr_merged_date) DAY) AS week_start,
         COUNT(*) AS prs_merged,
         AVG(pr_cycle_time) / 60.0 AS avg_cycle_hours
  FROM project_pr_metrics
  WHERE $__timeFilter(pr_merged_date)
    AND project_name IN ($project)
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT ai.week_start                   AS "Week",
       ai.ai_users                     AS "AI Active Users",
       ai.ai_lines                     AS "AI Lines Added",
       ai.ai_sessions                  AS "AI Sessions",
       ROUND(ai.ai_cost, 2)            AS "AI Cost (USD)",
       d.prs_merged                    AS "PRs Merged",
       ROUND(d.avg_cycle_hours, 1)     AS "Avg PR Cycle Time (h)"
FROM ai
INNER JOIN delivery d ON d.week_start = ai.week_start
ORDER BY 1 DESC

Developer join — AI usage next to that developer's PRs

panels.description: AI usage next to that same person's delivery. Blank PR columns mean identity did not match, NOT that the developer opened no PRs — check 'Identity' and the gaps table below. 'Accounts Merged' is how many `accounts` rows were treated as this person; PRs are summed across all of them, so someone active on two platforms is not undercounted.

targets.rawSql:
WITH member_emails AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT LOWER(ai.user_email) AS email
  FROM ai_activities ai
  LEFT JOIN accounts acc     ON LOWER(acc.email) = LOWER(ai.user_email)
  LEFT JOIN users u          ON LOWER(u.email)   = LOWER(ai.user_email)
  LEFT JOIN user_accounts ua ON ua.user_id = u.id
  JOIN pull_requests pr
    ON pr.author_id IN (ai.account_id, acc.id, ua.account_id)
  JOIN project_mapping pm
    ON pm.row_id = pr.base_repo_id AND pm.`table` = 'repos'
  WHERE pm.project_name IN ($project)
),
ai_agg AS (
  SELECT LOWER(user_email)             AS email,
         MAX(NULLIF(account_id, ''))   AS direct_account_id,
         SUM(lines_added)              AS ai_lines,
         SUM(num_sessions)             AS ai_sessions,
         SUM(estimated_cost_usd)       AS ai_cost,
         GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT provider ORDER BY provider) AS providers
  FROM ai_activities
  WHERE $__timeFilter(date)
    AND provider IN ($provider)
    AND user_email <> ''
    AND LOWER(user_email) IN (SELECT email FROM member_emails)
  GROUP BY 1
),
-- Identity: collect EVERY account belonging to this person, then
-- aggregate delivery across all of them.
--
-- Sources, any of which may contribute an account:
--   1. ai_activities.account_id, pre-resolved at convert time. It holds
--      only ONE id, so it can never represent someone with several
--      accounts — it is treated as one candidate, not the answer.
--   2. case-insensitive match on accounts.email. Contributes nothing for
--      private GitHub profiles, where accounts.email is ''.
--   3. org-plugin identity: users.email -> user_accounts -> accounts.id.
--      The only source that survives re-collection and the only one that
--      works when emails are absent.
--
-- Why union rather than pick-one: a person routinely owns several rows in
-- `accounts`. Some are duplicates that author nothing (gitextractor mints
-- one keyed by commit email); others are genuinely active accounts on
-- different platforms, each with real PRs. Selecting a single 'best'
-- account handles the first case but silently discards delivery from the
-- second — a developer with 2 GitLab and 4 GitHub PRs would report 4.
-- Summing over every account is correct for both: empty duplicates
-- contribute zero and drop out on their own.
accts AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.email AS email, acc.id AS account_id
  FROM ai_agg a
  JOIN accounts acc
    ON acc.id = a.direct_account_id
    OR LOWER(acc.email) = a.email
    OR acc.id IN (SELECT ua.account_id FROM users u
                    JOIN user_accounts ua ON ua.user_id = u.id
                   WHERE LOWER(u.email) = a.email)
),
identity AS (
  SELECT a.email,
         COUNT(ac.account_id) AS account_count,
         CASE WHEN COUNT(ac.account_id) = 0 THEN 'UNMATCHED'
              ELSE 'matched' END AS match_state
  FROM ai_agg a
  LEFT JOIN accts ac ON ac.email = a.email
  GROUP BY 1
),
pr_agg AS (
  SELECT ac.email,
         COUNT(DISTINCT pr.id) AS prs_opened,
         COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN pr.merged_date IS NOT NULL
                             THEN pr.id END) AS prs_merged
  FROM accts ac
  JOIN pull_requests pr ON pr.author_id = ac.account_id
  LEFT JOIN project_mapping pm
         ON pm.row_id = pr.base_repo_id AND pm.`table` = 'repos'
  WHERE $__timeFilter(pr.created_date)
    AND pm.project_name IN ($project)
  GROUP BY 1
),
cycle_agg AS (
  SELECT ac.email,
         AVG(ppm.pr_cycle_time) / 60.0 AS avg_cycle_hours
  FROM accts ac
  JOIN pull_requests pr ON pr.author_id = ac.account_id
  JOIN project_pr_metrics ppm ON ppm.id = pr.id
  WHERE $__timeFilter(ppm.pr_merged_date)
    AND ppm.project_name IN ($project)
    AND ppm.pr_cycle_time IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT a.email                           AS "Developer",
       a.providers                       AS "AI Providers",
       i.match_state                     AS "Identity",
       i.account_count                   AS "Accounts Merged",
       a.ai_lines                        AS "AI Lines Added",
       a.ai_sessions                     AS "AI Sessions",
       ROUND(a.ai_cost, 2)               AS "AI Cost (USD)",
       p.prs_opened                      AS "PRs Opened",
       p.prs_merged                      AS "PRs Merged",
       ROUND(c.avg_cycle_hours, 1)       AS "Avg PR Cycle Time (h)"
FROM ai_agg a
JOIN identity  i ON i.email = a.email
LEFT JOIN pr_agg    p ON p.email = a.email
LEFT JOIN cycle_agg c ON c.email = a.email
ORDER BY a.ai_lines DESC

panels.title: Developer Fact Table (LEFT JOIN from the AI side)
Identity health — how much of the developer join actually lands

panels.description: Share of distinct AI user emails resolving to a DevLake account by any of the three tiers (pre-resolved account_id, accounts.email, or org-plugin users/user_accounts). Near 0% means the developer table will look empty even when AI data is fine — that is an identity problem, not a dashboard problem.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(
         100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE
           WHEN ai.account_id <> ''
             OR acc.id IS NOT NULL
             OR ua.account_id IS NOT NULL
           THEN LOWER(ai.user_email) END)
         / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT LOWER(ai.user_email)), 0)
       , 1) AS "Identity Match %"
FROM ai_activities ai
LEFT JOIN accounts acc ON LOWER(acc.email) = LOWER(ai.user_email)
LEFT JOIN users u      ON LOWER(u.email)   = LOWER(ai.user_email)
LEFT JOIN user_accounts ua ON ua.user_id = u.id
WHERE $__timeFilter(ai.date)
  AND ai.provider IN ($provider)
  AND ai.user_email <> ''

panels.title: Identity Match % (all projects)

panels.description: AI users unmatched by ALL THREE identity tiers. Fix these by adding the person to the org plugin: PUT /plugins/org/users.csv (Id,Name,Email) then map them with PUT /plugins/org/user_account_mapping.csv — note that endpoint only reads its Id and UserId columns and silently ignores the rest, and it CANNOT set accounts.email. Also expect gh-copilot users here: that plugin stores a GitHub LOGIN in user_email, not an email.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT LOWER(ai.user_email)                          AS "Unmatched AI User",
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ai.provider ORDER BY ai.provider) AS "Providers",
       SUM(ai.lines_added)                           AS "AI Lines Added",
       ROUND(SUM(ai.estimated_cost_usd), 2)          AS "AI Cost (USD)",
       MAX(ai.date)                                  AS "Last Active"
FROM ai_activities ai
LEFT JOIN accounts acc ON LOWER(acc.email) = LOWER(ai.user_email)
LEFT JOIN users u      ON LOWER(u.email)   = LOWER(ai.user_email)
LEFT JOIN user_accounts ua ON ua.user_id = u.id
WHERE $__timeFilter(ai.date)
  AND ai.provider IN ($provider)
  AND ai.user_email <> ''
  AND (ai.account_id IS NULL OR ai.account_id = '')
  AND acc.id IS NULL
  AND ua.account_id IS NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 3 DESC
